The key detail is that `xfailed_key` is initialized during setup (before the test body runs), and `pytest_runtest_call` evaluates it *before* yielding to the test. A marker added inside the test body therefore misses both evaluations, so reporting sees no xfail. I’ll reproduce this first and inspect the surrounding report logic and xfail test suite before deciding whether to refresh markers after `yield` or at report time.

A marker added inside the test body therefore misses both evaluations, so reporting sees no xfail. A marker added inside the test body therefore misses both evaluations, so reporting sees no xfail. The key detail is that `xfailed_key` is initialized during setup (before the test body runs), and `pytest_runtest_call` evaluates it *before* yielding to the test. A marker added inside the test body therefore misses both evaluations, so reporting sees no xfail. I’ll reproduce this first and inspect the surrounding report logic and xfail test suite before deciding whether to refresh markers after `yield` or at report time.

The key detail is that `xfailed_key` is initialized during setup (before the test body runs), and `pytest_runtest_call` evaluates it *before* yielding to the test. A marker added inside the test body therefore misses both evaluations, so reporting sees no xfail. I’ll reproduce this first and inspect the surrounding report logic and xfail test suite before deciding whether to refresh markers after `yield` or at report time.
